newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo Nobel says pill sales picked up in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Akzo Nobel says pill sales picked up in Q2.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Thursday sales volumes of its low-dosage contraceptive pill, hit by a scare over thrombosis risks last year, picked up in the second 1997 quarter.
"Finally again we have a growth in sales volumes of our third generation contraceptive pills," Akzo's finance director Jean den Hoed told a results news conference.
"It's only two percent growth, but it shows the tide has turned," he said.
Akzo earlier reported second quarter net profit up 25 percent at 459 million guilders.
Den Hoed said Akzo was still losing volume in the United Kingdom and Germany where authorities have imposed restrictions on prescribing, but that the U.S decline was bottoming out.
Akzo's pharmaceuticals arm Organon was optimistic of gaining registration for its low-dosage pills in Japan after clearing most of the administrative hurdles, he added.
"We hope that registration will be achieved this year, although we cannot say for sure," Den Hoed said.
